title: Chili con carne
intro: Beef and kidney beans slow-simmered with cumin and smoked paprika: thick and warming.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and soften the chopped onion and pepper over medium heat.
steps.label: Soften

steps.t: Add the garlic and beef, turn up the heat and brown it, breaking it up, until no longer pink and lightly colored.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Stir in cumin, paprika, cayenne, oregano and tomato paste for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add tomatoes, water and salt, bring to a boil, set the lid ajar and simmer gently, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Simmer

pressure.t: Add tomatoes, half the water and salt, lock the pressure cooker lid and cook 20 minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: Add the beans and cook uncovered until the chili is thick and rich.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Taste, adjust salt and heat and let it rest off the heat before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Melt in a square of dark chocolate at the end: it rounds out the flavor without tasting of it.
Serve with white rice, sour cream and tortilla chips, or spooned over a baked potato.
It's even better the next day and freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Shakshuka
intro: Eggs gently poached in a pepper, tomato and harissa sauce, served in the pan.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a wide lidded pan and cook the onion and sliced peppers over medium heat until soft and sweet.
steps.label: Peppers

steps.t: Add sliced garlic, cumin, paprika and harissa and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes, season with salt and simmer uncovered until thickened.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Make 4 hollows in the sauce with a spoon, crack an egg into each and season lightly.
Cover and cook on low until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Scatter over chopped herbs and pepper and bring the pan straight to the table.

tips.t: Serve with warm bread or pita to mop up the sauce (skip it to keep the dish gluten-free).
Crumble 80 g of feta over the sauce before covering for an even tastier pan.

title: Jambalaya
intro: Louisiana rice with chicken, smoked sausage and shrimp, all cooked in one pot.

steps.t: In a wide lidded pot, brown the sliced sausage in the oil until golden, then lift it out.
steps.label: Sausage

steps.t: In the same fat, brown the diced chicken until golden on all sides, then lift it out.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Add diced onion, pepper and celery and cook until soft.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add garlic, paprika, thyme, oregano, cayenne and bay for 1 minute, then pour in tomatoes and hot stock (store-bought is fine) and bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, return chicken and sausage, salt, cover and cook on low without stirring; the chicken finishes cooking in the rice.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Tuck the shrimp into the rice, cover and cook until pink and the rice is tender.
steps.label: Shrimp

steps.t: Turn off the heat and rest, covered. Remove the bay leaves and top with sliced scallions.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Don't stir while the rice cooks: it stays fluffy and forms a light crust on the bottom.
A dash of Louisiana-style hot sauce at the table is practically mandatory.

title: Italian beef stew with potatoes
intro: Beef braised slowly in wine and stock with potatoes: Italy's winter Sunday dish.

steps.t: Cut the meat into 4 cm chunks and pat dry. Brown it in batches in hot oil in a heavy pot until well crusted.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Lower the heat, add chopped onion, carrot and celery and let them soften.
steps.label: Soften

steps.t: Return all the meat, pour in the wine and let it bubble off, scraping the bottom.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Add tomato paste, rosemary, bay and hot stock (store-bought or cube is fine) to cover. Put the lid on and cook on low.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Add tomato paste, herbs and stock to half-cover the meat. Lock the lid and cook 25 minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: Add peeled potato chunks and salt. Keep cooking, covered, until the potatoes are tender and the meat falls apart.
steps.label: Potatoes

pressure.t: Add the potato chunks and salt, lock the lid again and cook 8 more minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: If the sauce is too thin, uncover for the last minutes. Turn off the heat and let it rest before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Don't crowd the pot when browning: the meat should sizzle, not stew in its juices.
It's even better the next day: reheat gently with a ladle of stock.
Instead of potatoes, add peas for the last 15 minutes, as they do in Tuscany.

title: Vegetable and chickpea tagine
intro: Squash, carrots and chickpeas stewed with Moroccan spices and dried apricots.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a tagine or heavy casserole and soften the sliced onion over medium heat.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add garlic, ras el hanout, ginger and turmeric and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add carrots cut in thick sticks and squash in large chunks and turn them in the spices.
Add tomatoes, stock (store-bought is fine), chickpeas, halved apricots and salt. Cover and simmer until the veg are tender.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Uncover and let the sauce reduce over medium heat.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Finish with chopped coriander and toasted almonds.

tips.t: Serve with steamed couscous; for gluten-free, with rice or quinoa.
A chopped preserved lemon rind stirred in at the end gives the authentic aroma.

title: Ciambotta
intro: Southern Italy's summer stew: potatoes, peppers, eggplant and zucchini in tomato.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a wide pot and soften the sliced onion and garlic over medium heat.
steps.label: Soften

steps.t: Add the potatoes in 2 cm cubes and stir them around in the oil.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Add pepper strips and eggplant cubes, salt and cook, stirring often, until they start to soften.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add zucchini chunks, chopped tomatoes and basil. Cover and cook on low until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick.
steps.label: Stew

steps.t: If it's too liquid, uncover for the last minutes. Turn off and let it rest: it's even better warm than hot.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Crack 4 eggs over the hot stew for the last 5 minutes and cover: it becomes an even heartier meal.
Serve with toasted country bread, and shaved aged pecorino for those who want it.

title: Feijoada, black bean and pork stew
intro: Brazil's Saturday stew: black beans slow-cooked with pork and smoked meats.

steps.t: The night before, soak the beans in plenty of cold water for at least 12 hours; then drain and rinse them.
Separate the ribs, cut the beef into 4 cm cubes, the bacon into chunks and the sausage into 1 cm slices.
In a large pot, cook the bacon in the oil until the fat runs, then add the ribs and beef and brown them well.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Add the chopped onions and garlic and cook, stirring, until soft.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add the beans, bay leaves and water, bring to a boil and simmer covered, stirring now and then and adding hot water if needed.
steps.label: Simmer

pressure.t: Add the beans, bay leaves and water, lock the pressure cooker and cook 40 minutes at pressure; let it release naturally.

steps.t: Add the sausage and cook uncovered until the beans are creamy and the broth thickens.
steps.label: Sausage

pressure.t: Open, add the sausage and cook uncovered for 15 minutes until the broth thickens.

steps.t: Mash a ladle of beans and stir back in to thicken; remove the bay leaves and season with salt and pepper.
Serve with white rice, farofa, couve greens and orange slices to cut the richness.

tips.t: With carne seca, paio and linguiça from a Brazilian shop it's Rio-style: desalt the carne seca 24 hours.
Feijoada completa: white rice, farofa, couve à mineira, vinagrete and orange slices.
It's even better the next day: make it ahead and reheat gently with a splash of water.

title: Bò kho, lemongrass beef stew
intro: Beef braised with lemongrass, star anise and carrots, for dunking warm bread.

steps.t: Finely chop the garlic, ginger and 1 lemongrass stalk. Bruise the other 2 stalks with the back of a knife and cut into chunks.
Cut the beef into 4 cm cubes, mix with the chopped aromatics, five-spice, sugar and half the fish sauce and marinate 30 minutes.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: In a heavy pot heat the oil with the chopped shallots and paprika, then brown the beef over high heat for 8 minutes.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the star anise, cinnamon, lemongrass and water. Bring to a boil and skim.
Cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beef is almost tender.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Lock the pressure cooker lid and cook 30 minutes from when it hisses, then release the pressure.

steps.t: Add the carrots in large chunks and the rest of the fish sauce and cook uncovered 30 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Carrots

pressure.t: Add the carrots and the rest of the fish sauce and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until tender.

steps.t: Remove the spices and lemongrass and season with fish sauce, sugar and pepper. The beef should fall apart under a spoon.
Serve in bowls with cilantro and lime wedges, and warm baguettes for mopping up the sauce.

tips.t: The real red comes from annatto seeds, sold in Asian shops: fry 1 tsp in the oil instead of the paprika.
In southern Vietnam half the water is coconut water, for a sweeter, rounder sauce.
It's even better the next day; serve leftovers over rice noodles instead of bread.

title: Kimchi jjigae, kimchi and pork stew
intro: Ripe kimchi, pork and tofu in a spicy red broth, brought bubbling to the table.

ing.n: well-fermented cabbage kimchi, with its juice

steps.t: Slice the pork belly thinly, cut the kimchi into 3 cm pieces, the onion into wedges and the tofu into 1 cm slices.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot and fry the pork over medium-high heat until it sizzles in its own fat.
steps.label: Pork

steps.t: Add the kimchi, minced garlic, gochugaru and sugar and stir-fry until the kimchi softens and smells toasty.
steps.label: Kimchi

steps.t: Pour in the water, kimchi juice, gochujang and soy, add the onion, bring to the boil and simmer, covered, over medium-low heat.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Lay the tofu on top and simmer until heated through and tinted red.
steps.label: Tofu

steps.t: Add the spring onions in pieces, taste and adjust the salt. Bring the pot to the table with a bowl of rice each.

tips.t: The older and sourer the kimchi, the better the jjigae; if it's young, add a teaspoon of rice vinegar.
Swap the pork for a can of tuna in oil and you have chamchi kimchi-jjigae.
Reheated the next day it's even tastier; add a splash of water.

title: Doenjang jjigae, soybean paste stew
intro: A rustic soybean paste stew with tofu, courgette, potato and mushrooms, served bubbling.

steps.t: Put the kombu in the cold water in a pot and heat slowly; take it out as soon as the first bubbles appear.
steps.label: Stock

steps.t: Meanwhile cut the potato and courgette into 1.5 cm cubes, the onion into pieces, the mushrooms into slices and the tofu into 2 cm dice.
Dissolve the miso in the stock by pressing it through a sieve with a spoon, then add the gochujang and minced garlic.
Add the potato and onion and simmer.
steps.label: Potato

steps.t: Add the courgette, mushrooms and tofu and cook until the potato is tender.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add the sliced chilli and spring onion, cook for 1 minute and serve piping hot with rice.

tips.t: With real doenjang from a Korean shop the flavour is deeper and earthier than with miso.
Many families use a stock of kombu and dried anchovies: more savoury, though no longer vegan.

title: Nikujaga, beef and potato simmer
intro: Japan's ultimate home dish: beef and potatoes in a sweet and savoury broth.

steps.t: Cut the potatoes into large chunks and keep them in cold water. Cut the onion into wedges, the carrot into chunks, the beef into 5 cm pieces.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the beef until it changes colour, then add the onion, carrot and drained potatoes.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Pour in the dashi (instant is fine), sake, mirin and sugar. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Lay a disc of baking paper with a hole in the middle right on the surface and simmer for 10 minutes over medium-low heat.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Add the soy sauce and cook for 10 more minutes, until a skewer slides into the potatoes easily.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Add the peas and cook for 2 minutes, stirring as little as possible so the potatoes don't break up.
steps.label: Peas

steps.t: Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes: as it cools, the potatoes soak up the flavour.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve in bowls with a little of the broth, alongside plain rice.

tips.t: The paper drop lid (otoshibuta) keeps the broth circulating and the potatoes whole.
In the Kanto region it's often made with pork; if your Asian shop has them, add 200 g shirataki.
Even better the next day: keeps 3 days in the fridge, reheat gently.
